model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of samples across varying levels of ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity. The chart is divided into seven slices representing different combinations of ambiguity levels. These include "Ambiguity std2," "Single-LLM," "Single-LLM-annotated," "Single-LLM-unannotated," "All," and two categories labeled "2" and "Il."  The slices are colored in varying shades of blue and purple. The "Ambiguity std2" slice represents approximately 3%, the "Single-LLM" slice approximately 4%, the "Single-LLM-annotated" slice is approximately 6%, the "Single-LLM-unannotated" slice is 7%, the "All" slice represents 23%, the slice labeled "2" is approximately 46%, and the slice labeled "Il" accounts for roughly 24% of the total. The chart includes a legend identifying each slice’s label and, at the top, displays a value of 0.88, 0.89, and 0.90 alongside the x-axis numbers 1, 2, and 3.  The slices appear visually ordered from largest to smallest in size.
